title: Part Four, Chapter 2: Xtah and Xpuch

verses.t: And here begins the stealing of the men of the peoples by Balam-quitzé, Balam-acab, Mahucutah and Yquibalam. And then came the killing of the people whom these took; they went only by ones or twos when they were taken, and then they went to sacrifice them before Tohil and Avilix; and then they poured the blood on the road and threw their heads on the roads. And the peoples said, "The jaguar ate them," and they said this because they saw that the tracks were made like the tracks of jaguars; and the four did not show themselves. And already they had stolen many people. And the peoples noticed it too late, and said, "Can it be Tohil and Avilix who comes in here and seeks out only the captains? Where can their houses be? We shall follow the tracks," said all the peoples. And then they consulted among themselves, and then they began to follow the tracks of the chiefs, but they could not trace them; they saw only the tracks of deer and of jaguars. And the first tracks could not be traced, but were turned around so that they would be lost; and the road was not clear, and a drizzle began, a drizzle and a mist, and it became very muddy and drizzled; and this is what was seen before the peoples. And tired of searching, they gave up following, because the being of Tohil, Avilix and Hacavitz was very great. And the peoples from whom they were killing went far off to the top of a mountain; and from this began the stealing of the people who die on the roads and are sacrificed before Tohil, Avilix and Hacavitz; and the four kept their children safe there on the mountain. And Tohil, Avilix and Hacavitz went about like three boys, and so they looked like boys, only by the miracle of the stone. And so they were seen at a river, bathing at the water's edge; and that bath of Tohil was called their appearing. And many times the peoples saw them, and then they would vanish from them when they were seen by the peoples. And then there was news of where Balam-quitzé, Balam-acab, Mahucutah and Yquibalam were, and then the peoples consulted so that they might be killed.

And first the peoples wished to consult about overcoming Tohil, Avilix and Hacavitz; this the chiefs proposed before the peoples. And all were called and summoned, and not one or two of the tribes stayed behind, but all gathered and were called. And then they consulted, and said, asking one another, "What shall we do to overcome these upstarts of the Quiché? For our vassals are being finished off, and it is not clear how the men are lost. Shall we be finished off by this stealing when it is done? Or is this great anger of Tohil, Avilix and Hacavitz, and is this Tohil to be our god in slavery? Will it not be possible for us to overcome them? Are we not many men? And these upstarts of ours are few." This is what they said when they all gathered. And one part of the peoples spoke and said, "Where did they see them bathing in the river every day? And if this is Tohil, Avilix and Hacavitz, we shall defeat them first, and there the overcoming of the great ones will begin." This is what half of them said when they spoke. And they said, "What shall we overcome them with?" The rest said, "In this way," they said, "we shall overcome them: since they are young men when they appear at the river, let two maidens go who are very beautiful, very fair maidens, and let desire for them come upon them." "Very well," they all said. "Let us look for two beautiful maidens," they said. And then they searched among their daughters; and truly they were very fair girls. And then they gave them their orders and said, "Daughters, go and wash the cloths at the river, and if three young men see you, undress before them; and if they desire you, win them. If they say to you, 'We shall go there where you are,' tell them yes. And when you are asked, 'Where have you come from, and whose daughters are you?', tell them, 'We are the daughters of the lords'; and tell them to give you a sign, and bring the sign they give you. And if they want to lie with you, give yourselves to them; and see that if you do not give yourselves, we shall kill you. And if you bring a sign, then our hearts will be well disposed toward you, and we shall love you; and if there is any sign, bring it." This is what they ordered the two maidens, who were called, the one Xtah and the other Xpuch. And the two maidens Xtah and Xpuch were sent to the river where Tohil, Avilix and Hacavitz bathed; and this was what the peoples devised.

And then they went and dressed and adorned themselves, and truly they were beautiful when they went to the river, to the bathing place of Tohil; and shamelessly and immodestly they washed; and the lords rejoiced over their two daughters whom they had sent. And arriving at the river, they began to wash, and both of them undressed, and each was working on her stone when Tohil, Avilix and Hacavitz came. And they came to the river, and pretended a little not to see the two maidens who were washing; and the maidens were at once ashamed when Tohil came. And in no way did Tohil desire the two maidens. And then they were asked, "Where do you come from?" it was said to the two maidens. "What is it you want, that you come here to our water?" And they said to them, "We have been sent here by the lords, and they told us, 'Go and see the faces of Tohil and speak with them, and likewise bring a sign that you have seen their faces'; so it was said to us." And when they had declared their errand, Tohil, Avilix and Hacavitz said, "Did the peoples want the maidens to fornicate with the naguals of Tohil?"

And they said again to Xtah and Xpuch, as the maidens were called, "Very well; a sign of our word shall go with you. Wait a little, and it will be given for you to take to the lords." And then the chiefs consulted, and it was said to Balam-quitzé, Balam-acab, Mahucutah and Yquibalam, "Paint on the three cloths the sign of your being, to go before the lords of the peoples; let the two maidens who are washing take it. Give it to them!" it was said to Balam-quitzé, Balam-acab and Mahucutah.

And then the three painted. And first Balam-quitzé painted the image of a jaguar, painting it on the cloth; and Balam-acab painted his image, which was an eagle, and painted it on the cloth; and Mahucutah, painting, painted nothing but hornets and wasps; his painting on the cloth was full of wasps all over. And the three finished their paintings; they painted on three folds. And then they went to give the cloths to Xtah and Xpuch, as they were called, and Balam-quitzé, Balam-acab and Mahucutah said to them, "This is the sign of your word and truth. Go, take it before the lords and tell them that Tohil truly spoke to you, and that this is the sign we bring. This you shall say to them; and give them the cloths to wear." This was said to the maidens when they were sent off. And then they went and carried the painted cloths; and as soon as they arrived, the lords rejoiced when they saw them and saw the maidens carrying what they had asked for hanging from their hands. "Did you see Tohil?" it was said to them. And they said, "We saw him." "Very well," said the lords, "and what sign have you brought? Is it really true?" And the lords thought it was a sign that they had sinned. And then the maidens spread out the painted cloths, and everywhere there were jaguars, everywhere eagles, and all hornets and wasps, painted on the cloth, which was glossy. And then the lords wanted to put them on, and they put on the first one, and the jaguar painted on the cloth did nothing to them. And then the lord put on the second, on which the eagle was, and it did nothing to him, and he turned about in it before all who had asked him to put it on. And then he put on the third, which was painted with hornets and wasps, and at once the hornets and wasps began to sting him all over his body; and he could not endure or bear the stings of the painted creatures, and the lord began to scream because of the creatures that Mahucutah had painted in the third painting. And the maidens Xtah and Xpuch were defeated and put to shame by the lords: "What cloths are these that you have brought? Where did you go to get them, you demons?" it was said to the maidens, when they were shamed and scolded. And so all the peoples were defeated by Tohil. And what they had wanted was for Tohil to go after the two maidens Xtah and Xpuch, and for them to have been harlots according to the will of the peoples, and for it to have been a temptation for the three; but it did not come about that Balam-quitzé, Balam-acab and Mahucutah, the naguals of men, fell.
